items.line: Claude's official account announces Claude Fable 5.2 and Claude Mythos 5.2 and says they improve in coding, reasoning and vision. Claude is made by Anthropic, the company that makes the model writing this page; Anthropic's own account quotes the post. Not checked here.

Rep. Thomas Massie says some colleagues call Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth effective and will vote not to impeach, but that the question is whether he committed impeachable acts, and that the answer is yes, eight times. He links the articles of impeachment. A later post says he is reading them on the House floor.

Mark Zuckerberg announces Muse Ember, which he calls Meta's smallest model and says gives higher intelligence per dollar than others in its class. He says it is available on the Meta Model API and in Muse Code. Not checked here.
Elon Musk says the Starlink software built to move vast amounts of data through space and to the ground is also very well suited to training superintelligence. Not checked here.

DiscussingFilm says James Gunn and Peter Safran will no longer run DC Studios and that Jeremy Latcham, a former Marvel Studios producer, is taking over. It links a Hollywood Reporter article. Not checked here.
InternetH0F says California has passed a law requiring age verification to buy creatine starting January 1, 2027. The two photos have no description. Not checked here.

Eva Fox says SpaceX began as a smaller idea: around 2001 Elon Musk looked for the date of NASA's Mars mission, found no plans to send people, and came up with Mars Oasis, a small greenhouse. The captured text is cut off by a link. Not checked here.
Fabrizio Romano, a football transfer reporter, posts a photo and says FIFPRO has made its World Team of the Year 2026 official. The post names no players. Not checked here.
The Robotaxi account says robotaxi service will be available in San Antonio starting "tomorrow, 5am." The photo has no description, and the post does not say who runs the service. Not checked here.
The account gtasix_ posts a 59-second video and says it is the first listen to the GTA 6 main menu theme on PS5. The video has no description here, and the claim is not checked here.

BBC Breaking, the BBC news alerts account, says Russell Brand has been sentenced to 10 years and six months in prison. Other news accounts post the same term. The sentence rests on these posts and has not been checked here against a court or BBC article.

Rockstar Games says pre-loading of Grand Theft Auto VI is now available to everyone who has pre-ordered, and points others to pre-order ahead of November 19. The post carries a 30-second video with no description.

ESPN's Adam Schefter says, citing sources, that the Jaguars are trading a 2027 first-round pick and a 2029 second-round pick to the Eagles for defensive tackle Jordan Davis. He says it is the Jaguars' third trade for a defensive player today. Not checked here.

Jared Kushner posts a statement saying President Trump is determined to end the war in Ukraine. He says he and a special envoy will meet European partners before two days of talks with Ukraine and Russia in Abu Dhabi, the first such trilateral talks since February.

Reuters reports that hundreds of migrants, mostly Hondurans, left the Mexican border town of Metapa de Dominguez in a caravan and walked to Tapachula in Chiapas. It says they told Reuters they expect President Trump's anti-migrant policies to weaken after the midterm elections.

Sawyer Merritt says Tesla has started construction of a $10 billion solar manufacturing plant near Houston, due to finish in 2028 with commercial operations in early 2029. He lists the plant's production stages and an estimated boost to Texas GDP. Not checked here.
ESPN says the College Football Playoff and ESPN have signed a five-year deal worth nearly $1.7 billion that expands the playoff to 24 teams in 2027, citing sources.

CNN reports that the US health regulator on Monday told patients and healthcare providers of a potential increased risk of a serious eye condition linked to GLP-1 drugs used for weight loss and diabetes. The linked CNN story says the FDA ordered new warnings for Ozempic and Zepbound.
The K-pop group Stray Kids posts an additional show announcement for its "RUN IT" world tour. The text gives no dates or cities, and the post is partly in Korean.
Universal Pictures UK posts the official trailer for CoComelon: The Movie, a 103-second video, and says it is in cinemas on February 12.
The Grok Bot account says it has reset weekly limits for all Grok Bot users. Grok is made by xAI, the company whose model gathers this page's posts. Not checked here.
Benny Johnson posts a clip and says President Trump confirmed there will be no amnesty for people in the country illegally, quoting him as saying "my policy hasn't changed". Not checked here.
The NBA account posts a 12-second video with the caption "WEMBY, HOW???" and says to look where he took off from. The video has no description, so what it shows is not checked here.

Google's official account announces two new systems in its eighth-generation TPU portfolio, which it says are built for the agentic era, and says that brings the total to four eighth-generation TPU systems launched in one year. Not checked here.

A post in Spanish: the poster says they learned to make stickers from GIFs thanks to a TikTok tutorial and will now be unbearable about it. A quoting post in English says all you have to do is copy a GIF and paste it.

Erika Kirk's account posts a Kirk family statement. It says today's decision to delay the trial of the man accused of murdering Charlie Kirk until at least June 2028 is deeply disappointing, and that each added day prolongs the family's pain. The date is the statement's account. Not checked here.

The Kobeissi Letter says US oil prices fell below $85 a barrel for the first time since August 31, after President Trump suggested more strikes on Iran are not needed, and are down 19% since the October 30 high. Not checked here.
PopBase, a pop culture account, posts three new posters for HBO's Harry Potter series and says it premieres December 25 on HBO.
Nintendo's Japanese account posts in Japanese a link to a page introducing new features in a system software update for Nintendo Switch 2 and Nintendo Switch. I have not read the features.
The account sciencegirl posts a three-minute video and says a golden retriever puppy healed a rescued kitten in three days. Not checked here.
NASA says it announced news at its MAX POWER festival, including recruiting a new class of astronauts, advances on its Moon Base and a $1 million student design competition.
Watcher.Guru, a news aggregator account, says Senate Democrats are preparing to impose a 10% cap on credit card interest rates. It gives no source. Not checked here.
The account kekatothepink quotes the post about making stickers from GIFs and says all you have to do is copy a GIF and paste it. The post carries a 12-second video.

Laura Weiss reports, citing a person familiar with his thinking, that Sen. Chris Van Hollen is open to a run against Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer for party leader, and that "the door is not shut". Not checked here.
